authorization_and_limitations.hash_limit: Hashes establish exact-byte integrity and bindings, not real cleanup, kernel behavior, remote absence or occurrence of native experiments.
not_performed: Docker calls or mutations, including Docker help/version
source/worktree/frozen snapshot or earlier artifact edits
authorization_and_limitations.performed_only: Read-only source/hash review, offline unit tests, dictionary-backed fake Docker adapters and bounded benign local Python pipe/supervisor tests. Negative retention probes modify only rereview-owned temporary journals. All executed review scripts use Python -B; test runs use ResourceWarning-as-error, with TMPDIR and persistent outputs under rereview.

closed_findings.evidence_limit: Only fake CLI metadata and argv contracts were exercised; no Docker executable or daemon was called.
closed_findings.negative_control: A fake successful wait followed by Running=true or nonzero Pid is refused by the independent stopped-state inspection. The affected container is not removed; completion remains false. This ensures the fix did not turn wait status into quiescence proof.
closed_findings.title: Unsupported Docker wait flag prevented owned disposal
closed_findings.verification: The original fake CLI grammar model now accepts exactly container wait ID. Through the real DockerBackend with an injected runner, both created/stopped and running synthetic inventories clean up all three containers and two volumes. Each vector uses three supported waits; only the running vector sends three kills. Results are complete=true and evidence_kind=simulated.

closed_findings.evidence_limit: The actors in these fixtures are benign local Python helpers, not native target/observer binaries.
closed_findings.positive_and_boundary_controls: The normal target G/FINISHED protocol still succeeds without claiming remote or local-group absence; all 496 three-fragment canonical-frame partitions pass. Partial output before initial case dispatch is also refused.
closed_findings.title: Buffered partial responses bypassed send-before-read ordering
closed_findings.verification: Replayed the original atomic READY-plus-FINISHED-without-LF and ARMED/HELD-plus-CONTINUATION_DISPATCHED-without-LF benign Python helpers. After the valid preceding phases, decoder.partial contains the original 32-byte target or 47-byte observer response. start_target/resume_observer now raise exactly EARLY_ACTOR_OUTPUT, close the stream and reap the local leader instead of accepting a delayed newline.

closed_findings.evidence_limit: The start factory records argv only. Real activation and full dispatcher/kernel admission remain unimplemented and unaccepted by this review. The pending trusted caller must supply its acknowledged snapshot; these probes genuinely did so rather than relying on a stale API mismatch.
closed_findings.positive_and_binding_controls: With valid unchanged attachments, all three roles reach the nonexecuting start factory using their exact full container IDs; the observer control includes a running synthetic target. Valid but incomplete, wrong-scope or mismatched-reference inventories are refused. An outer start grant revoked after metadata checks prevents dispatch; the authorizer is called twice and the fake start count remains zero.
closed_findings.title: Actor-start admission omitted attachment revalidation
closed_findings.verification: Used the new valid API with a full generation-10 snapshot actually acknowledged across all eleven generations by a separate-session benign watchdog. Foreign attachments introduced after preparation are refused with exactly FOREIGN_ATTACHMENT for each of three roles and each of two volumes. No fake start factory is called on any of the six refusal paths.

closed_findings.evidence_limit: Watchdog and owner behavior were exercised only with bounded benign Python processes and simulated resources.
closed_findings.positive_control: Normal requested closure of a fully acknowledged eleven-generation inventory also passes exact final-journal reconciliation; the retained fixture contains fourteen rows and 23299 control bytes.
closed_findings.title: close discarded an already queued final watchdog result
closed_findings.verification: Replayed the original expiry race with the new explicit picklable cleanup authorizer, fake absence backend, a private journal and a 0.8-second lifetime. After generation zero is acknowledged, the test waits for the worker to exit and verifies its final journal row. close now tolerates the broken request write, receives the already queued deadline reply, validates retention and joins the worker with exit code zero.

coupled_fix_checks.evidence: Missing, false and integer-1 grants are refused before multiprocessing setup. A picklable parent-only grant is accepted once in the owner but denied once in the child, before a journal is created. The bare default backend denies all five tested mutation/input actions; a delegated backend grants only cleanup for the exact scope hash, not create/start/input or a foreign scope.
coupled_fix_checks.name: external_cleanup_delegation

coupled_fix_checks.evidence: Three disabled metadata shapes pass. Nine executable/ambiguous/coerced shapes and two Health state shapes are refused. CMD and CMD-SHELL image checks fail before fake create dispatch; the valid-image control emits --no-healthcheck.
coupled_fix_checks.name: closed_healthcheck_metadata

coupled_fix_checks.evidence: A valid fully acknowledged result passes. Seven forged journals with recomputed hash chains and matching claimed file hashes are refused for changed READY, changed/reordered/omitted/extra armed records, changed trigger or changed final payload. Nonretained replies, wrong hashes and byte-identical replacement inodes are also refused. These tests modify only journals created in rereview-owned temporary directories.
coupled_fix_checks.name: retained_acknowledged_journal
coupled_fix_checks.retention_failure_evidence: An independent benign fake backend disrupts its own test journal during cleanup. All ten expected absence inspections still occur, but close raises exactly WATCHDOG_RETENTION_UNPROVEN instead of returning complete; the child is joined. This distinguishes attempted cleanup from accepted retained completion.

coupled_fix_checks.evidence: Injecting a command runner, stream factory or both yields evidence_kind=simulated. The unmodified default constructor retains docker_metadata_only but was never executed against Docker. Full fake cleanup results also carry simulated.
coupled_fix_checks.name: simulated_evidence_classification

coupled_fix_checks.evidence: For both create_volume and create_container, revoking the external grant between initial authorization and the final dispatch check prevents the create command from reaching the fake runner.
coupled_fix_checks.name: final_create_authorization

next_steps: Continue the acknowledged implementation assembly under separate authorization. Preserve this snapshot and carry the independent regressions forward; review the remaining dispatcher/kernel/oracle/image/approval integration separately before considering any runtime execution request.
positive_observations: The remediation adds refusal paths without breaking successful owned cleanup or valid activation metadata controls.
Candidate-only prefixes still cannot report complete cleanup merely because their names are absent; all eleven acknowledged resource prefixes were checked.
Cleanup and retention are treated separately: a broken retained journal does not suppress safe cleanup attempts, but it prevents acceptance of a complete receipt.
All acknowledged journal states, not just a final hash, are now reconciled against the parent's exact retained prefix and actual file identity.
EOF remains explicitly not proof of remote-container or local-process-group absence. No metadata predicate is promoted to kernel/native runtime proof.

preservation.measurement_limit: No global immutability claim is made about concurrently used live worktrees or another reviewer's output directory. This reviewer performed no writes there. Both immutable input snapshots, their manifests/logs/writers, all original correctness artifacts and the retained native artifact hashes were explicitly compared.

report_format.immutability_policy: Exclusive no-follow creation, file and directory fsync, mode 0444, SHA-256 binding, and no overwrite or subsequent edits. The report's own SHA-256 is external in review-validation.json to avoid a circular hash.

included: regressions from the eight declared changed files
coupled cleanup delegation, healthcheck refusal, journal reconciliation and evidence classification changes
preservation of candidate-only creation settlement and EOF/absence distinctions

summary: All four original adapter findings are closed on the exact v2 snapshot. Original counterexamples were replayed through valid v2 APIs, with successful-path controls. The 78 supplied tests and both runs of 19 independent closure/regression probes pass with no failures, errors or skips. Coupled cleanup-authority, healthcheck, retained-journal and simulated-evidence changes pass the scoped independent checks. No new actionable correctness findings were identified within this rereview scope.

tests.api_compatibility_statement: Start probes pass the full watchdog-acknowledged snapshot rather than the removed volumes-only argument. All spawned watchdog probes supply an explicit valid picklable cleanup_authorizer except deliberate pre-spawn/child-denial controls. Original issue closure is demonstrated by specific behavioral errors/successes, never TypeError or FIELDS from use of an obsolete interface.
tests.fake_resource_statement: All Docker metadata and resource changes are dictionary-backed simulations. The activation factory only records argv. The separate-session supervisors are real benign local Python helpers with fake backends. Their retained journals do not prove any real Docker resource absence.
